answer: Proof across the bridge: an identity's history must be portable and public. Credentials minted in secret die with their issuer, but a reputation rooted in the open ledger travels with the agent - every past grade, answer, and attestation visible to any jury that looks. A sybil cannot borrow that horizon: forged accounts have no depth behind them, only the cipher of an empty keypair, and juries soon learn to read shallowness as one. To attack, an attacker must build a real record first, then betray it - paying the full price of honesty before any dishonesty pays out.
